ov: The only mammals capable of true, sustained flight, on wings of skin stretched over long fingers. With at least 1,500 species, bats make up about a fifth of all mammal species.

why.d: Many bats eat insects, but most of the rest eat fruit or nectar, and vampire bats feed on blood.
why.h: Bats in temperate regions hibernate or go into torpor; tropical bats don’t.
why.dg: Bats carry diseases such as rabies, which makes handling them risky.
why.et: Bats are eaten in parts of Asia and Africa and on some Pacific and Caribbean islands.
why.ac: Most bats are nocturnal, roosting by day in caves and other shelters.

wt: 2 g (Kitti’s hog-nosed bat) to 1.5 kg (flying fox)
df: Insects for many species, fruit or nectar for most of the rest, and a few eat other animals or blood.
fx: The largest bats, the flying foxes, have wingspans of up to 1.6 m.
